title: Rudy Tomjanovich raves about Houston Rockets' acquisition of Kevin Durant: 'I can't wait' - NewsBreak
text: Kevin Durant isn't officially a member of the Houston Rockets yet, but his acquisition has already drawn rave reviews from one of the central figures in franchise history. Rudy Tomjanovich , the All-Star forward who later coached the Rockets to their two NBA championships in 1994 and 1995, was excited about what the implications of Durant's pending acquisition from Phoenix meant for the franchise moving forward. “We have one of the greatest players of all time coming in and I think it’s going to be great chemistry and balance on the team,” Tomjanovich said Wednesday during the Rockets' NBA draft watch party at Toyota Center. “When we talk about the team for the last couple of years, the first thing you thought was how young we are, and so bringing in a veteran like him gives more of a mix of youth and experience because he’s a veteran who’s still hungry and a great player. I can’t wait.” Tomjanovich praised Durant’s ability to move without the ball and thinks he’ll be a great fit for the Rockets. “Kevin’s not a ball-stopper. The ball doesn’t stop when it gets to him,” said Tomjanovich, who was the coach when Houston made another blockbuster trade, acquiring Clyde Drexler in 1995. “He’s a willing passer and shoots well off of screens, so I think he’ll fit in beautifully.” He also cited the importance of Durant’s ties to coach Ime Udoka from their time together with the Brooklyn Nets. “It’s so important that he and Udoka have a history with one another,” he said. “As a coach, Udoka knows what he’s getting from his player and that they have a good relationship makes it even more encouraging.” Steve Francis and Moochie Norris were other Rockets alumni on hand Wednesday who also endorsed the move. Francis said Durant’s acquisition will bring some more energy to the fan base and attract eyeballs to the young talent on hand. “Last year was great, getting the second seed in the playoffs, but everybody was still talking about the Lakers, Golden State and Minnesota,” Francis said. "So I think having an established MVP and player like KD here will help energize everybody inside and outside the building. Hopefully it gets the whole city hype, and we see a lot more highlights next year.” According to Norris, Durant’s experience and knowledge will pay dividends for the Rockets' budding stars. “Getting somebody like KD is unbelievable,” Norris said. “His accolades, his reputation, how he plays the game, he’s just about hooping and winning. I know the young guys are looking forward to getting around him, picking his brain, and seeing what it will take to bring their own games to the next level and what it will take for the team to make that next jump.” The draft party was a bit of an oddity for Rockets fans, whose team agreed to trade this year's No. 10 and 59 picks along with Jalen Green and Dillon Brooks to the Suns for Durant. At No. 10, Houston selected Duke center Khaman Maluach on behalf of Phoenix with the trade still pending. The draft concludes with the second round Thursday at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, N.Y, Some fans were OK with the fact the Rockets were without a pick for this year and believe Durant’s addition is a good thing for the team, despite the cost. “I’m OK with no first-round pick,” said Amon Simon, a fan of over 30 years. “B ecause we just got our guy on top of the young guns we have coming up. We didn’t have a guy like him on this team, and I think KD can get us over the hump and make us championship contenders."
